newsitem.title: USA: Nintendo says won't cut N64 price for now.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo says won't cut N64 price for now.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said Monday it will not cut the price of its Nintendo 64 video game machine for now, in the wake of Sony Corp's 25-percent price cut on the PlayStation.
Nintendo is sold out of its new video game machine through at least April and does not need to cut prices, said George Harrison, Nintendo vice president of marketing.
"We will sit and examine the situation for now," Harrison said.
On Monday, Sony said it cut the price of its PlayStation video game machine by $50 to $149. The Nintendo 64 sells for $199.
Analysts said Sony's move could trigger a video-game price war.
